The team was led by 1st-year head coach [[Kim English (basketball)|Kim English]], and played their home games at [[Amica Mutual Pavilion]] in [[Providence, Rhode Island]] as a member of the [[Big East Conference]]. ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Friars]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 21–12, 13–7 in Big East play to finish in a tie for fourth place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] to [[2022–23 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 11 seed in the East region. There they lost to [[2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in the first round. On March 10, 2023, [[Ed Cooley]] left the school to take the head coach job at [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{Cite web |date=2023-03-20 |title=Cooley hired to lead Georgetown's 'new chapter' |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35904201/sources-georgetown-expected-hire-providence-ed-cooley |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On March 23, the school named [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] head coach [[Kim English (basketball)|Kim English]] the team's new head coach.{{Cite web |title=Providence hires Kim English: George Mason coach tabbed to lead Friars after Ed Cooley leaves for Georgetown |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/providence-hires-kim-english-george-mason-coach-tabbed-to-lead-friars-after-ed-cooley-leaves-for-georgetown/ |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=CBSSports.com |date=March 23, 2023 |language=en}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
